evidence.title: Find the movement behind
evidence.highlight: the moment you want to coach.
evidence.copy: CourtFlux follows players, teams and the ball across time, then builds that movement into basketball state. The current P2 layer can structure ball control, possession changes, loose-ball sequences, shot attempts and candidate pass, turnover and rebound events.

faq.question: Do I need an analyst to use CourtFlux?
faq.answer: No. The Coach workflow is aimed at individual coaches who want a faster way to organise and review basketball video evidence.

faq.question: Can I analyse opposition footage as well as my own team?
faq.answer: Yes, provided you have the right or authority to submit and analyse the footage. The analysis workflow is based on the video and match context rather than requiring the source to be your own team.

faq.question: Do I need a complete roster before analysing a game?
faq.answer: No. Home and away team names are enough to start. Roster and jersey details can remain optional until player-level identity is needed.

faq.question: What can I expect from the beta today?
faq.answer: The current system tracks players, teams and the ball and includes a P2 basketball-state layer for ball control, possession changes, loose-ball sequences, shot attempts and candidate pass, turnover and rebound events. Formal event and attribution accuracy is still being validated against reviewed human ground truth.

faq.question: Is my uploaded game video kept forever?
faq.answer: No. Directly uploaded source video is scheduled for deletion after 60 days. The derived analysis results and statistics remain available in your workspace.
